name: Okubo Vance Slim Bomber
description:
Okubo Vance is a Tier 3 lifestyle brand with a clean aesthetic — no logos on the outside, minimal branding on the inner label, clothes that look expensive without announcing it. The Slim Bomber is their perennial bestseller: a satin-finish nylon outer shell with ribbed knit cuffs and collar, a clean zip placket, and an interior in quilted silk-analog that feels cool against skin. It comes in a rotating seasonal palette — this season offers a muted terracotta, a pewter grey, and a deep forest green. The silhouette is fitted without being restrictive, sitting just below the hip.

It is the kind of jacket that works over a dress shirt for a late meeting or over a plain tee on the weekend. Tier 3 office workers and mid-level corp employees wear it as a statement of quiet taste. It does not have any tech features. It is simply a very good-looking bomber at a price that requires saving up or expensing.
what_it_says: You have taste and the budget to act on it. You are not trying to impress anyone in particular, which is itself a kind of impression.
worn_by: people who dress well on a considered budget
story_hooks: A character is wearing the exact same bomber in terracotta as the person they are supposed to surveil — they have to decide whether to change or lean into it
Okubo Vance quietly discontinued a colorway after one appeared in surveillance footage of a high-profile assassination; wearing that color now carries unspoken weight
An Okubo Vance bomber in mint condition, three seasons old, is found in an abandoned Tier 2 apartment — the previous tenant was clearly not Tier 2
